[[File:Azai-jinja in Ichinomiya ac (1).jpg|thumb|250px|right|Torii]]

{{nihongo|'''Azai Shrine (Ichinomiya)'''|浅井神社 (一宮市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}{{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}{{ill|Azai|Q11556970|qid=Q11556970|lt=Azai-chō}}. {{nihongo|'''Azai Shrine (Ichinomiya)'''|浅井神社 (一宮市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== Overview ==
Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was village shrine. It is also written as '''淺井神社'''.

It is the “Azai Shrine” of {{ill|Nakashima district|Q780420|qid=Q780420}} in {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki shrine register}}. According to the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, there are two Azai Shrines in Nakajima District, Owari Province. This article describes the Azai Shrine in Ichinomiya City. For the Azai Shrine in Inazawa City, see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Azai Shrine}}.

Although this area belongs to {{ill|Haguri District|Q1032507|qid=Q1032507}} of Owari Province, Azai Shrine is an Engishiki shrine of Nakajima District, Owari Province. Similarly, there is a theory that “{{ill|Iwato Shrine|ja|石刀神社|qid=Q11585184}},” an Engishiki shrine of Nakajima District, Owari Province, corresponds to {{ill|Iwato Shrine|ja|石刀神社|qid=Q11585184|lt=Ishito Shrine (Azai-chō, Ichinomiya City)}}. There is also a theory that the Engishiki shrine “Kosai Shrine” of Nakajima District corresponds to {{ill|Ozeki Shrine|ja|小塞神社|qid=Q11459557}}. As this region is an area frequently affected by flooding of the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}}, it is said that the district boundaries since the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} are not clearly defined; therefore, this area may also have belonged to Nakajima District. The area where Azai Shrine stands is near the borders of Haguri District, Nakajima District, and {{ill|Niwa District|ceb|Niwa-gun|es|Distrito de Niwa (Aichi)|fa|شهرستان نیوا، آیچی|fr|District de Niwa|id|Distrik Niwa, Aichi|it|Distretto di Niwa|ja|丹羽郡|ko|니와군|pl|Powiat Niwa|ru|Нива (уезд)|sr|Област Нива|tl|Distrito ng Niwa, Aichi|uk|Повіт Ніва|vi|Niwa, Aichi|zh|丹羽郡|qid=Q1347719}}.

== History ==
Founded in {{ill|563|ab|563|af|563|am|563 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|563|ar|563|ary|563|ast|563|az|563|azb|۵۶۳ (میلادی)|bar|563|be|563|be_x_old|563|bg|563|bn|৫৬৩|bpy|মারি ৫৬৩|br|563|bs|563.|ca|563|cdo|563 nièng|ceb|563|ckb|٥٦٣|crh|563|cs|563|cv|563|cy|563|da|563|de|563|el|563|eml|563|eo|563|es|563|et|563|eu|563|fa|۵۶۳ (میلادی)|fi|563|fo|563|fr|563|fy|563|ga|563|gan|563年|gd|563|gl|563|he|563|hi|563|ht|563 (almanak jilyen)|hu|563|hy|563|id|563|io|563|it|563|ja|563年|jv|563|ka|563|kk|563 жыл|ko|563년|la|563|lb|563|lij|563|lmo|563|lt|563 m.|map_bms|563|mdf|563|mhr|563|mk|563|mr|इ.स. ५६३|mrj|563 и|ms|563|mzn|۵۶۳|nah|563|nap|563|nds|563|new|सन् ५६३|nl|563|nn|563|no|563|nso|563|oc|563|or|୫୬୩|os|563-æм аз|pl|563|pnb|563|pt|563|qu|563|ro|563|ru|563 год|rue|563|sa|५६३|sah|563|scn|563|sd|563ع|sh|563.|shn|563|si|563|sk|563|sl|563|sq|563|sr|563|su|563|sv|563|sw|563|tg|Соли 563|th|พ.ศ. 1106|tk|563|tl|563|tly|563|tr|563|tt|563 ел|uk|563|ur|563ء|uz|563|vec|563|vi|563|war|563|wuu|563年|xmf|563|zh|563年|zh_min_nan|563 nî|zh_yue|563年|qid=Q33782}} (24th year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792}}).

The shrine buildings stand atop a kofun (Azai Shrine Kofun), from which items such as gold rings and iron arrowheads have been excavated. This area contains many small kofun collectively known as the Azai Kofun Group, and {{ill|Ozeki Shrine|ja|小塞神社|qid=Q11459557}}, also an Engishiki shrine, likewise has its shrine buildings on a kofun.

The shrine has deep connections with water, and it is said that one of the Three Famous Springs of Owari, “Azai no Onkoi,” once existed here. The name Onkoi (温故井) remains at Onkoi Pond in {{ill|Azaiyama Park|ja|浅井山公園|qid=Q11556931}} south of Azai Shrine (a former tributary of the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}}).

During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Hachiryūsha, and the enshrined deity was believed to be a {{ill|Dragon god|Q1206058|qid=Q1206058}}.

In {{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}} (2nd year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}), it was renamed back to Azai Shrine, and in {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (5th year of Meiji) it became a village shrine.

== Access ==
* About an 8-minute walk from the “Azai” bus stop on the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|Q6810397|qid=Q6810397}}.
* From {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850|lt=Meitetsu}} {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Q1137838|qid=Q1137838|lt=Nagoya Main Line}} / {{ill|Meitetsu Bisai Line|Q901005|qid=Q901005|lt=Bisai Line}} {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Q2856589|qid=Q2856589}} or {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|lt=JR}} {{ill|Tōkaidō Line (JR Central)|Q11235139|qid=Q11235139|lt=Tōkaidō Main Line}} {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Q871495|qid=Q871495}} (Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station Bus Terminal, platform 3), take a bus bound for “Miyata Hongō.”
